html:
The Anambé are a small Tupi-Guarani people of Pará in Brazil, living on the Cairari river in the Moju basin south of Belém.

They were among the Tupi peoples of the lower Amazon, near the Tembé and Guajajara. Contact with settlers and epidemics in the 1900s left only a few dozen people. Few of them still speak their language.
sum: The Anambé are a small Tupi-Guarani people of Pará in Brazil, living on the Cairari river in the Moju basin south of Belém.
